goals.goal: TinyTask, as controller of customer-account personal data and processor of customer task data in its B2B SaaS platform, maintains a documented process for regularly testing, assessing, and evaluating the effectiveness of the technical and organisational measures ensuring the security of that processing, and reviews its data-protection impact assessment whenever a change in the risk represented by the processing operations is identified.
goals.adjustment: Restated from the five-regulation, AI-inclusive baseline to TinyTask's 8-person managed-cloud SaaS context: AI-specific attack categories (data poisoning, model evasion, etc.) and NIS2/DORA/AI Act legs excluded (no AI/ML systems; not a financial entity; not an essential/important entity); the "regularly" cadence is discharged by a documented periodic testing programme scaled to the Art. 32(1) preamble factors; DPIA review trigger retained as the Art. 35(11) material-change condition.

goals.goal: TinyTask, as manufacturer of a product with digital elements (SaaS platform with web and mobile interfaces) placed on the EU market in the default product class, ensures the product is made available without known exploitable vulnerabilities and maintains a continuing identification process — including a machine-readable software bill of materials covering at least the top-level dependencies and a vulnerability register — throughout the product's support period, exercising the constructive-knowledge due-diligence baseline.
goals.source: CRA Annex I Part I (2)(a); CRA Annex I Part II (1)
goals.adjustment: Restated from the five-regulation baseline to TinyTask's CRA manufacturer role on a default-class (self-assessment) SaaS product: NIS2/DORA/AI Act legs excluded (not applicable per fact sheet); the R2 constructive-knowledge baseline (inquiry-resistant, Annex VII §3 due-diligence floor) retained as the identification standard; SBOM scope limited to top-level dependencies per Annex I Part II (1); no AI-specific threat-model overlay (no AI/ML systems).
